source_registry.findings: The fitted historical 80%-reliability cyber task horizon doubled in about 4.7 months on the selected suite. Later results exceeded the earlier fitted trend.
source_registry.limitations: Restricted tasks, partly estimated human baselines, scaffolding and saturation limit extrapolation. This is not a doubling time for real attacks or societal harm. Reuses evidence also reviewed in the AI assessment, not an independent replication.

source_registry.review_scope: Publication and official release; Chapter 1 selected sections including external interest and financing statistics; PDF pp.13 and 29 inspected as images.

source_registry.title: OECD, Global Debt Report 2026: Sustaining Debt Market Resilience Under Growing Pressure
source_registry.review_scope: Official publication page and full HTML executive summary. Underlying microdata and all annexes were not reanalysed.
source_registry.findings: OECD central-government gross borrowing was about USD17 trillion in 2025; around USD13.5 trillion was refinancing, while net requirements were around USD3.5 trillion. Markets remained resilient in 2025; issuance shifted toward shorter maturities, raising refinancing exposure.
source_registry.limitations: Gross issuance is not net new borrowing. USD29 trillion for governments and corporations in 2026 is a forecast with a different coverage. A maturing bond is not a missed payment, nor an essential-service failure. Maturity and investor composition matter alongside levels.

source_registry.title: Farah-Yacoub, Graf von Luckner and Reinhart, The Social Costs of Sovereign Default
source_registry.review_scope: Official indexed NBER abstract and primary Harvard author-institution publication summary. Full NBER paper download not retrieved; later repository revision dates are not treated as a new independent study.
source_registry.findings: After methodological exclusions the stated sample includes 221 default episodes over 1815–2020. Augmented synthetic controls and local projections estimate persistent output gaps and adverse social outcomes. The abstract reports an 8.5% per-capita-output gap within three years and nearly 20% after a decade relative to comparators.
source_registry.limitations: Working-paper status; historical observational identification, not random assignment. Outcomes have different data coverage, and the abstract does not establish that all health indicators span all 221 episodes. Comparator gaps are not literal destruction of the same fraction of the economy or an irreversible global loss.

source_registry.title: Asonuma, Chamon, Morito and Sasahara, Trade Dynamics in Sovereign Debt Crises
source_registry.review_scope: Official abstract plus PDF introduction, classification and selected methods. PDF internal authorization page says October 2025; official publication date is November 14. Figure-based numeric estimates are not used.
source_registry.findings: 194 restructurings of privately held external sovereign debt in 76 countries over 1975–2019; 115 post-default and 79 preemptive. source_registry.limitations: Working paper, not institutional policy or a randomized comparison. Adjustment for observed selection does not eliminate unobserved confounding. Trade values or import/GDP ratios are not themselves medicine, calorie or energy delivery metrics.

_meta.source_dependence: Inherited registries retain their original review status. New biodiversity evidence can share underlying studies and is not counted as independent merely because it appears in different publications. Blacksell/Dhawan papers have overlapping authors, incident history and scope. Wittmann 2025/2026 share a study lineage and tool-development participants. International assessment may synthesize the same studies. Eleven references are not eleven independent effect estimates. WMO, IGCC and the Global Carbon Budget share some observations, methods and contributors. Assessment summaries and original papers are not independent replications; alternative temperature datasets also share underlying observations. Cyber review: The clinical appendix and replication record are parts of CY_R03. NCSC/AISI work overlaps AI-review evidence. ENISA reports share institutional inputs. Publication counts are not independent replication counts. IMF reports share data and institutional assumptions; World Bank data may feed other analyses. Historical default/restructuring studies can use overlapping episodes. DE_R08 and DE_R10 describe the same roundtable process. Bibliographic count is not independent replication count.
_meta.runtime_import: Import as a source map with mu/lo/hi, not an obs evidence overlay. A new custom source-map upload replaces the previous custom layer. Use the cumulative 48-entry file to retain prior reviews and clear any active evidence overlay.
_meta.metadata_warning: Runtime v1.2.9 may ignore or drop the additive evidence-schema fields during custom import/export. This JSON preserves them as provenance; the numerical mu/lo/hi inputs remain v1.9.0-compatible.
_meta.interval_semantics: lo/hi are analyst plausibility anchors. Existing beta/log-normal samplers approximate 90-percent widths; coverage is not calibrated, asymmetric endpoints are not hard bounds, and cap/clamp operations can alter sampled means. mu is a central judgment, not a guaranteed post-clamp median.

amr.reason: Retain the moderate continued-pressure scenario: lo 0.003, nominal center 0.020, hi/cap 0.035. Current evidence supports persistent pressure with mixed trajectories and meaningful mitigation, but does not identify a global latent functional-pressure growth rate. These values are pre-existing scenario conventions, not mortality, isolate or antibiotic-consumption CAGR. No preferred crossing year was used to choose them. Test near-flat, slow and rapid alternatives separately; positive-only runtime omits recovery.

It is not temperature CAGR, CO2 emission growth, carbon-sink change, mortality growth or annual failure probability. Keep the common-class choice for comparability and test alternative rates separately; no calendar year is targeted. The raw URL is empty because no source directly calibrates the numerical rate.
climate.role: Growth of autonomous latent pressure; susceptibility to dependency loss can evolve even when an independent process year is censored. Retained event/regime arrival models remain separate heuristic assumptions.

cyber.reason: Retain moderate conditional prior lo 0.003, nominal centre 0.020 and hi 0.040 with runtime threat cap 0.045. No reviewed source identifies this latent annual rate. The event engine also sets its initial hazard to 2*g*priority/threshold; this additional mapping is uncalibrated. No raw reporting-growth or capability-CAGR reconversion and no target calendar date.
cyber.role: Growth of autonomous latent pressure; susceptibility to dependency loss can evolve even when an independent process year is censored. Retained event/regime arrival models remain separate heuristic assumptions.

debt.reason: Retain the shared slow scenario prior: lo=0.001, nominal mu=0.010, hi=0.025, execution cap=0.030. This is conditional annual relative growth of autonomous latent pressure on essential-service finance, not debt/GDP growth, an observed default hazard or a social-loss CAGR. No cited source identifies this number; alternatives must be stress-tested without tuning to a desired date. Direct engine-unit flag is an execution guard only. Positive-only growth omits stabilisation and recovery.
debt.role: Growth of autonomous latent pressure; susceptibility to dependency loss can evolve even when an independent process year is censored. Retained event/regime arrival models remain separate heuristic assumptions.

epistemic.reason: Fresh evidence supports meaningful current pressure but not a globally identified accelerating functional-loss rate. Human discernment remains substantial and several interventions improve accuracy or trust. Slow replaces moderate as the central continued-pressure scenario; 0.020 remains a required sensitivity case.
epistemic.role: Growth of autonomous latent epistemic functional pressure; not annual misinformation prevalence or trust decline.

fragmentation_gov.reason: Strong current institutional strain coexists with continued rule use, new agreements and inter-organizational adaptation. Slow replaces moderate as the central autonomous functional-pressure scenario; higher growth remains a sensitivity case.
fragmentation_gov.role: Growth of autonomous latent coordination-failure pressure; not growth in the number of disputes, organizations or trade restrictions.

geopolitics.reason: Record conflict counts and greater interstate confrontation support material continued pressure, while spending growth slowed and conflict-management outcomes remain heterogeneous. Moderate is retained as a pressure scenario, not an observed event-frequency growth rate.
geopolitics.role: Growth of autonomous latent escalation pressure; event-process arrival remains a separate uncalibrated engine mapping.

minerals.reason: Realized disruptions and concentration support persistent pressure, but supply response, stocks, substitution, recycling and diversification argue against using commodity-demand CAGR as latent failure growth.
minerals.role: Autonomous latent mineral-supply functional pressure, not demand or price CAGR.

nuclear.reason: Modernization, high operational alert and weaker arms-control constraints support continuing pressure, but neither arsenal data nor treaty outcomes identify annual nuclear-war hazard growth.
nuclear.role: Growth of latent containment/war-pressure prior; not warhead or event-frequency growth.

oceans.reason: Accelerating physical stress and compound ocean-state change support sustained pressure, but heterogeneous biological responses, management and restoration argue against a rapid universal failure prior.
oceans.role: Autonomous latent marine functional pressure, not temperature, pH, oxygen, biomass or fishery-stock CAGR.

pandemics.reason: More frequent outbreaks and worsening emergence drivers support positive pressure; expanded surveillance, rapid response and containment improvements argue against fitting a rapid pandemic-failure growth rate.
pandemics.role: Autonomous latent pandemic functional pressure, not outbreak or pandemic-arrival frequency.

pollution.reason: Persistent pollutants and rising plastics support positive pressure, but pollutant-specific trends, regulation, source control and remediation make a single moderate growth prior too strong.
pollution.role: Autonomous latent pollution functional pressure, not a pollutant-mass or mortality CAGR.

soils.reason: Widespread and worsening degradation supports continued pressure, but soil processes and restoration responses operate on highly different rates and no common empirical functional-loss CAGR is identified.
soils.role: Autonomous latent soil functional pressure, not degraded-area, erosion, SOC or yield-loss CAGR.

space.reason: Rapid orbital occupation and debris accumulation support persistent pressure, but service resilience and remediation mean inventory or Health-Index growth cannot be used directly as functional-loss growth.
space.role: Autonomous latent space-service pressure, not satellite/debris CAGR.

supply.reason: Severe shocks demonstrate vulnerability, but rerouting, inventories, production response and persistent GVC integration argue against a moderate autonomous failure-growth prior.
supply.role: Autonomous latent essential-supply pressure, not trade, price or freight CAGR.

water.reason: Freshwater storage, groundwater and per-capita availability trends support continuing pressure, while service expansion, efficiency, infrastructure and documented aquifer recovery argue against a moderate autonomous functional-loss growth prior.
water.role: Autonomous latent water-service pressure, not withdrawal, drought or groundwater-level CAGR.

authoritarian.reason: Broad institutional deterioration supports persistent pressure, while widespread stability and documented reversals argue against a faster autonomous functional-failure prior.
authoritarian.role: Autonomous latent accountable-governance functional pressure; not regime-count or democracy-index CAGR.

ai.functional_failure: Loss of effective human control or correlated deployment failures persistently impair multiple essential decision, communication or infrastructure functions beyond practical human fallback. Benchmark performance or AI adoption alone is not this boundary.

amr.functional_failure: Loss of effective infection prevention and treatment undermines routine, emergency and invasive care across linked health systems, with inadequate therapeutic substitutes and persistent excess burden. Selected resistance prevalence alone is not the boundary.

autonomousw.functional_failure: Inadequately controlled autonomous targeting or decision support causes sustained escalation and civilian protection failures that impair essential functions beyond practical human override. Deployment counts or any use of autonomy do not establish this boundary.

biodiversity.functional_failure: Persistent loss of key regulating, renewal and stabilising ecological functions, including functional abundance and interactions, across connected systems despite remaining species.

bioengineered.functional_failure: A severe engineered biological event overwhelms prevention, treatment and continuity arrangements across linked populations, causing persistent disruption of health care and other essential services beyond feasible containment. Research output or technical capability alone is not failure.

climate.functional_failure: Sustained loss of sufficiently stable climatic conditions for ecological renewal and essential human production across multiple connected regions, beyond feasible adaptation; not global uninhabitability.

cyber.functional_failure: Sustained, coordinated or common-mode loss of digital control, communications or payments prevents essential-service delivery across connected regions beyond practical backups and timely restoration. Complaint counts, data breaches or monetary losses alone do not establish this boundary.

debt.functional_failure: Debt-service or refinancing disruption persistently constrains essential public services, working capital and payments across linked economies after feasible restructuring and substitution are insufficient. A high debt-to-GDP ratio alone is not failure.

displacement.functional_failure: Protection, shelter, food, water, health care and livelihood systems cannot provide sustained basic access to forcibly displaced people and affected communities after feasible inclusion and assistance. People seeking safety are not themselves the threat.

economic.functional_failure: Interacting payment, credit, employment and production disruptions persist across major connected economies such that normal substitution and stabilization cannot maintain essential goods and services. A recession or asset-price correction alone is not this boundary.

epistemic.functional_failure: Reliable warning, verification and trusted coordination channels become inadequate for sustained collective response to essential-service threats. Low trust, disagreement or misinformation volume alone does not establish functional failure.

fragmentation_gov.functional_failure: Cross-border institutions and implementation arrangements cannot sustain coordinated protection of essential functions during interacting crises, and feasible national or issue-specific substitutes are insufficient. Vetoes and policy disagreement alone do not satisfy this boundary.

geopolitics.functional_failure: Escalating interstate confrontation persistently disrupts essential supply, infrastructure and coordinated crisis response across connected regions beyond available rerouting and de-escalation capacity. Military expenditure increases alone are not the failure boundary.

minerals.functional_failure: Persistent inability to supply suitable materials or processing outputs required by multiple essential industrial chains after available inventories, substitution and diversified supply are exhausted.

nuclear.functional_failure: A severe nuclear-conflict pathway produces sustained, widespread loss of food, health care, physical safety and infrastructure beyond feasible substitution or timely recovery. This boundary is not an increase in warhead inventories or any isolated nuclear-related incident.

oceans.functional_failure: Persistent loss of recruitment, trophic transfer and ecological renewal across connected marine systems, compromising habitat maintenance or food provision even while substantial marine biomass remains.

pandemics.functional_failure: Widespread epidemic disease exceeds treatment, workforce and continuity capacity across connected regions for a sustained period despite feasible containment, impairing health care and essential services. Detection of an outbreak alone is not this boundary.

pollution.functional_failure: Persistent loss of effective exposure control, safe environmental media and pollutant-processing capacity that produces major health or ecosystem impairment beyond feasible treatment and prevention.

soils.functional_failure: Persistent loss of soil fertility, moisture regulation and productive support across connected food-producing regions, beyond feasible agronomic and restoration buffers.

space.functional_failure: Sustained loss of essential satellite navigation, timing, communication or observation cannot be covered by terrestrial or orbital substitutes, impairing linked infrastructure and coordination. Growth in tracked objects or loss of isolated satellites alone is not this boundary.

supply.functional_failure: Essential energy, food, medicine or critical production inputs remain unavailable across connected regions after feasible inventory drawdown, rerouting and substitution, impairing multiple essential services. Tariffs or nominal trade changes alone are not functional failure.

water.functional_failure: Persistent inability to deliver sufficient usable water and environmental flows across connected populations, production systems and ecosystems after feasible treatment, storage and transfers.

authoritarian.functional_failure: Sustained suppression of accountable decision-making and corrective information prevents affected societies from maintaining equitable essential-service access and coordinating recovery. Autocratic classification alone is not functional failure.

evidence_grading_methodology.principle: Keep threat-level scientific evidence, numerical parameter calibration, source authority/methodological quality, model-component evidence and dependency-edge evidence separate. Do not infer one from another.

threat_scientific_evidence_scale.A: Strong, direct and multiply supported evidence for the stated threat dimension/mechanism at the relevant scale.
threat_scientific_evidence_scale.B: Strong or moderate evidence with some extrapolation, scope limitation or indirect inference.
threat_scientific_evidence_scale.C: Limited, heterogeneous or predominantly scenario/analogue evidence for the stated threat dimension.
threat_scientific_evidence_scale.D: Predominantly hypothetical or weakly supported claim.
threat_scientific_evidence_scale.U: Not separately assessed or insufficient evidence.

parameter_calibration_scale.A: Parameter or mapping directly empirically calibrated and externally validated for the model estimand.
parameter_calibration_scale.B: Well-supported empirical or validated proxy mapping with limited model adaptation.
parameter_calibration_scale.C: Evidence-anchored analyst/expert mapping; source supports direction/mechanism but not the exact normalized value.
parameter_calibration_scale.D: Uncalibrated model convention, latent scenario prior, heuristic coefficient or abstract model anchor.

source_authority_scale.A: Peer-reviewed scholarly source, major official scientific/statistical institution, consensus body or primary high-authority technical record.
source_authority_scale.B: Recognized specialist research/evaluation/academic source with narrower authority or non-peer-reviewed institutional status.
source_authority_scale.C: Lower-authority secondary/commercial/advocacy source or weak provenance.

source_methodological_scale.A: High-strength synthesis or strong large-scale empirical design for its own estimand.
source_methodological_scale.C: Useful but indirect, scenario/model-based, narrow, working-paper, technical or institutional analysis.
source_methodological_scale.D: Normative/legal/status/process source not designed for scientific effect-size or parameter estimation.

evidence_grading_methodology.aggregation_policy: Grades are ordinal. They must not be arithmetically averaged across unlike evidence dimensions. Threat overall_grade is an explicit qualitative synthesis, not A=4/B=3/C=2/D=1 averaging.
evidence_grading_methodology.source_metadata_verification_note: Source authority/methodological grading used the registry metadata, recorded access scope/limitations, and targeted verification of missing displacement/economic records. It is AI-assisted assessment, not external peer review.

legacy_strength_policy.meaning: Legacy `strength` classifies the evidentiary/mapping posture of an individual numerical parameter. It must not be displayed as the overall scientific evidence grade of the threat.

threshold_cascade_family.rationale: Threshold activation and cascading propagation on networks are well-established model families. The specific q_i + kappa_i D_i >= 1 implementation is a transparent project adaptation, while its coefficients are not directly calibrated.

directed_dependency_network.rationale: Directed interdependence and weighted transmission are standard systemic-risk concepts. The Apocalypse Clock topology is an evidence-informed project graph whose complete causal structure is not empirically identified.

dependency_equal_share_weights.rationale: Weighted directed edges are established, but equal 1/n incoming shares are a transparent neutral prior when relative effect sizes are unknown, not an empirically estimated causal allocation.

propagation_one_year_lag.rationale: Time delays are legitimate dynamic-network parameters. A universal one-year delay is a model-resolution convention, not a measured cross-domain causal lag.

background_dep_factor.rationale: Network exposure/centrality effects are established concepts, but the retained depFactor formula and depAlpha=0.22 are project-specific and not externally calibrated.

cascade_susceptibility_kappa.rationale: Target-specific cascade susceptibility is standard in threshold models; the exact ordinal mapping of interdependence and governance failure into kappa is project-specific.

nhpp_event_family.rationale: Time-varying Poisson first-arrival processes are standard event-hazard models. The family is established, but the Apocalypse Clock event parameters are not fitted to event-time data.

event_hazard_mapping.rationale: The current lambda0 = 2*g*priority/threshold and use of the same g for subsequent hazard growth are project-specific mappings; factor 2, baseline intensity and trend are not independently identified.

service_top_event_or_rule.rationale: OR-type top events, AND gates and k-out-of-n structures are standard reliability/fault-tree constructs. Which essential-service condition should define the Apocalypse Clock top event, and the 0.50 threshold, are project semantics rather than measured global constants.

overlap_group_max.rationale: Using max within an overlap group is a transparent anti-double-counting rule but encodes complete overlap/redundancy within that group rather than an empirically estimated overlap coefficient.

first_passage_absorbing_marker.rationale: First-passage analysis is a standard way to model time to initial threshold crossing. The Clock deliberately stops at first functional crossing and does not model post-crossing recovery; this is an endpoint definition, not a claim of permanent collapse.

parameter_evidence.rationale: The cited evidence supports the relevant phenomenon, mechanism, direction, magnitude context or persistence, but it does not directly estimate the exact normalized 0–5 Apocalypse Clock score and interval.

authoritarian.growth_rate.source: Analyst scenario synthesis anchored to International IDEA 2026, V-Dem 2026 and recovery evidence
authoritarian.growth_rate.note: The slow 0.010 continued-pressure prior is retained. Long-running deterioration in checks, expression and rule of law supports persistent pressure, but country classifications change discontinuously, 81% of IDEA country-factor observations are stable, and documented U-turns show endogenous recovery. No reviewed source identifies an annual growth rate of functional institutional failure.
authoritarian.growth_rate.calibration_note: Direct effective pressure prior already in engine units. It is not growth in the number of autocracies, population living under a regime type, freedom-index decline, election result or annual probability of political transition. Positive-only growth cannot represent democratic recovery.

parameter_evidence.rationale: The cited evidence informs pressure direction, drivers or plausible scenarios, but does not directly estimate this annual latent functional-pressure growth rate. The numerical lo/mu/hi are scenario priors.

authoritarian.threshold.source: Expert model anchor informed by International IDEA/V-Dem institutional-function evidence
authoritarian.threshold.note: Functional failure means sustained suppression of accountable decision-making and corrective information prevents affected societies from maintaining equitable essential-service access and coordinating recovery. A regime label, election result, low democracy score or institutional dispute alone is not this boundary. The 8.7 value remains an abstract model anchor.
authoritarian.threshold.model_anchor_note: Abstract functional impairment boundary; not a regime classification, democracy-index score or electoral threshold.
